project.topic: What if every Man on Earth disappeared?
project.title: What If Every Man on Earth Disappeared?
project.audience: General international audience of teens and adults, nontechnical; no prior science knowledge assumed
project.core_question: What would happen to people and to nature if every man and boy on Earth vanished in a single instant?
project.viewer_takeaway: Humanity would survive, grieving and smaller, while oceans and cities briefly fell quiet; men would return within nine months as tens of millions of baby boys, and twenty years later the oldest man alive would be twenty.

scientific_model.baseline_reality: The world of 2026 (UN World Population Prospects 2024, medium projection): about 8.30 billion people, about 4.17 billion male and 4.13 billion female; about 132 million births a year with roughly 105 boys born per 100 girls. ILO modelled estimates put employment at about 70% of men and 46% of women aged 15+, so men hold about 60% of jobs. Women are about 67% of health and care workers but were only about 1.3% of seafarers in 2021. Traffic, shipping and industry are major sources of noise and vibration that wildlife measurably responds to.
scientific_model.counterfactual_change: At one instant (T0) every living person counted as male in UN population statistics (men and boys of all ages, about 4.17 billion people) vanishes painlessly. Bodies and worn clothing disappear; anything held, carried or being operated stays behind. Nothing else changes: women and girls, pregnancies already underway (whatever the baby's sex), frozen sperm, eggs and embryos, all animals and all infrastructure remain.
assumptions: 'Men and boys' means the UN 'male' category used for demographic arithmetic; the film does not model gender identity and acknowledges that intersex and transgender people exist.
The removal is instantaneous, painless and one-time; no reversal, replacement population or new reproductive technology is assumed.
Pregnancies already underway continue regardless of the baby's sex; frozen sperm, eggs and embryos in banks and clinics are unaffected.
All non-human animals, including male animals, are unaffected.
Infrastructure is physically intact at T0: lights and automated systems keep running until they fail, run out of fuel or are shut down, so city lights stay on in every post-T0 shot.
Secondary casualties from accidents and failures in the first hours are acknowledged in the model but neither quantified nor depicted.
Story-world times (T0, 'overnight', 'weeks later', '+20 years', '+40 years') are labeled on screen wherever the picture jumps in time.

Real-world analogs (Bay of Fundy after 9/11 in 2001; COVID-19 lockdowns in 2020) are presented as measured evidence of how the ground and wildlife respond to less human activity, not as predictions of exact magnitudes in this scenario.
causal_chain: T0: about 4.17 billion people vanish; humanity falls to about 4.13 billion, roughly the size of the world in 1975.
About 60% of the employed workforce is gone at once, very unevenly: health and care keep most staff (about 67% women) while cargo shipping loses almost all crews (about 1% women).
Within hours to days many vehicles, ships, machines and industrial processes stop or are shut down, while lights and automated systems keep running for a while.
Human-made noise and vibration drop sharply; measured analogs show ground vibration quieting by up to 50% (2020) and ship noise falling about 6 dB (2001).
Wildlife responds quickly: right whale stress-hormone levels fell with less ship noise, and city sparrows sang softer yet were heard about twice as far.
Births continue for nine months from pregnancies already underway: about 99 million babies, about 50 million of them boys.
Afterward births plunge, sustained mainly by frozen sperm, until the post-T0 boys grow up; twenty years on, the oldest man alive is about twenty.
Societies grieve, retrain and rebuild; activity and noise return over years, and over decades street life could look ordinary again.
uncertainties: How fast survivors restore transport, energy, food supply and shipping, which sets how long the quiet lasts.
Secondary casualties and infrastructure failures in the first hours and days.
The share of pregnancies carried to term under extreme shock and disrupted care (the 50 million estimate would fall).
The size and usability of global frozen-sperm stocks and how quickly insemination and IVF capacity could scale.
Large regional variation in workforce shares (women's share of health workers, for example, differs widely by country and role).
The wildlife evidence comes from single regions and species (Bay of Fundy right whales; San Francisco Bay Area white-crowned sparrows); responses elsewhere may differ.
Social, economic and political outcomes, and the population path after twenty years, are not modeled.

claims.statement: In 2026 the world has about 8.30 billion people: about 4.17 billion males (men and boys) and 4.13 billion females.
claims.reasoning: UN World Population Prospects 2024 medium-variant projection for 2026 (about 4,171.5 million males and 4,129.2 million females), as tabulated from WPP 2024.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Narration rounds to 'over four billion men and boys'; the on-screen callout reads '4.17 BILLION' with the tag 'men and boys · UN WPP 2024'.

claims.statement: Removing all males leaves about 4.13 billion people, close to the world population of 1975 (about 4.07 billion).
claims.reasoning: 8.30 B minus 4.17 B is about 4.13 B; WPP 2024 gives about 4.07 B for 1975, within about 1.5%.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Say 'about its size in 1975'; the ribbon chart is tagged 'SCHEMATIC · UN WPP 2024' and its curve uses WPP annual totals, not hand-drawn values.

claims.statement: Men hold about six in ten of the world's jobs (ILO 'employment', meaning work for pay or profit).
claims.reasoning: ILO modelled estimates for 2024: about 70% of men and 46% of women aged 15+ are employed; with similar adult populations, men's share is about 0.70 / (0.70 + 0.46), or about 60%. ILO's 2023 labour force was about 2.2 B men and 1.4 B women.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Use 'paid jobs' and the '6 of 10' token meter tagged 'ILO 2024 · derived'; never imply women do less work overall, because unpaid care work, mostly done by women, is excluded from this statistic.

claims.statement: With roughly 60% of workers gone at once and survivors in shock, many vehicles, machines, ships and industrial processes would stop or be shut down within hours to days.
claims.reasoning: Follows from CL03 and from how operator-dependent systems behave: dead-man controls, safety shutdowns and fuel exhaustion.
claims.presentation_guardrail: The port diorama is tagged ILLUSTRATIVE with a 'lights stay on' chip; no crashes, fires or casualties are depicted; 'overnight' is spoken as a figure of speech for 'within a day'.

claims.statement: During the 2020 COVID-19 lockdowns, high-frequency seismic noise from human activity fell for months by up to 50%, most strongly at surface seismometers in populated areas.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Narration says 'in places, by half'; tag '2020 LOCKDOWNS · MEASURED' and bracket 'up to −50% · some stations'; the trace is a schematic animation, not real station data.

claims.statement: Losing about 4.17 billion people at once would be the largest loss of human life in recorded history, by more than an order of magnitude.
claims.reasoning: Even the highest commonly cited death tolls of history's deadliest pandemics and wars are in the low hundreds of millions.
claims.presentation_guardrail: No historical death tolls on screen; grief is shown through absence and comfort, never bodies, panic or crying sounds.

claims.statement: Nearly every family would lose someone.
claims.reasoning: About half of all people vanish, and almost every household or extended family includes men or boys.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Say 'nearly every', not 'every'; the window tableaux show varied family types, including an older woman who lives alone.

claims.statement: Women make up about 67% of health and care workers worldwide, so on average hospitals would keep most of their staff.
claims.reasoning: The joint ILO–WHO analysis (2022) reports that women account for 67% of health and care workers worldwide.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Callout '67%' tagged 'health & care workers who are women · ILO–WHO 2022'; do not imply every hospital would be fine, since some specialties and countries are majority male.

claims.statement: Women were about 1.28% of the world's seafarers in 2021, mostly on cruise ships and ferries, so cargo ships would lose almost all their crews.
claims.reasoning: BIMCO/ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2021 (reported by Marine Log). The 2026 report's executive summary describes growth concentrated among female officers but gives no updated share; even a doubling would leave crews overwhelmingly male.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Callout '≈1%' tagged 'seafarers who are women · 2021 (BIMCO/ICS)'; the empty bridge is calm, with the ship on autopilot and no collisions.

claims.statement: After 11 September 2001, reduced ship traffic in Canada's Bay of Fundy lowered underwater noise by about 6 dB (especially below 150 Hz), and North Atlantic right whales' baseline stress-hormone metabolites fell.
claims.reasoning: Rolland et al., Proc. R. Soc. B 279:2363–2368 (2012), using faecal glucocorticoid metabolites.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Tag 'BAY OF FUNDY, CANADA · 2001 · MEASURED'; present it as one region and one species; the hormone bar is labeled schematic.

claims.statement: If most merchant shipping stopped for weeks or months, low-frequency ship noise along busy sea lanes would drop sharply, and noise-sensitive marine animals could benefit for a while.
claims.reasoning: Analogy to CL10, scaled to the near-total crew loss implied by CL09.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Tag 'WEEKS LATER · ILLUSTRATIVE' on the propeller shot; sound rings tagged SCHEMATIC.

claims.statement: During the spring 2020 shutdown in the San Francisco Bay Area, urban noise fell to levels typical of the mid-1950s; white-crowned sparrows sang more softly but with higher performance, and their songs could be heard about twice as far.
claims.reasoning: Derryberry et al., Science 370:575–579 (2020); the researchers' calculation of a roughly doubled communication distance is reported by Eos and the University of Tennessee.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Tag 'SAN FRANCISCO BAY AREA · 2020 · MEASURED'; ring radii labeled 'radii illustrative'; callout '≈2×'.

claims.statement: Under this thought experiment, pregnancies already underway continue; naturally about 105 boys are born for every 100 girls (about 51% boys).
claims.reasoning: The biological sex ratio at birth is about 105:100 (UN WPP 2024 via Our World in Data; the 2026 world tabulation gives 105.3). Continuation of pregnancies is a stated assumption.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Never color-code babies (no pink or blue); the newborn shot shows no sex; the narration carries the 'sons' fact.

claims.statement: About 132 million babies are born each year, so roughly 99 million births would follow in the nine months after T0, about 50 million of them boys.
claims.reasoning: UN WPP 2024 estimates about 132.4 million births in 2025; 0.75 × 132 M is about 99 M; × 0.51 is about 50 M boys. Likely somewhat lower if shock and disrupted care raised pregnancy losses.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Narration says 'tens of millions'; callout '≈50 million' tagged 'boys born within 9 months · estimate'; birth glints tagged ILLUSTRATIVE, not one glint per birth.

claims.statement: After those nine months, nearly all new conceptions would depend on frozen sperm in banks and clinics, so births would plunge far below today's 132 million a year until the boys born after T0 reach adulthood.
claims.reasoning: Follows from the definition; assisted reproduction can use stored sperm, but stocks and clinic capacity are tiny relative to global births.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Post-T0 birth bars are thin and hatched, tagged 'births mostly via sperm banks · estimate'; no number is stated for them.

claims.statement: Every male alive after T0 is born after T0, so twenty years later the oldest man on Earth would be about twenty.
claims.reasoning: Direct consequence of the definition: the first post-T0 boys are born within days of T0 from pregnancies already underway.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Callout 'OLDEST MAN: 20' appears only when the year chip reads '+20 YEARS'; the pyramid is tagged SCHEMATIC.

claims.statement: Humanity would survive: about 4.13 billion women and girls plus tens of millions of newborn boys, with reproduction continuing at reduced levels; the population would keep shrinking for at least a generation while societies retrain and rebuild.
claims.reasoning: Combines CL02, CL14 and CL15; women already work in every occupation and could train new workers, though shortages would be severe in male-dominated sectors.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Show grief (a memorial) and rebuilding (women lineworkers) together; no utopian or dystopian framing; no claims about politics or economics.

claims.statement: Over later decades street life could look ordinary again: younger generations would have a near-normal sex balance, while older age groups would remain mostly women for a lifetime.
claims.reasoning: Applies the 105:100 birth ratio (CL13) to post-T0 cohorts; how busy cities become depends on recovery and choices.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Narration uses 'could'; the final crowd is a story-world illustration at about '+40 YEARS' with no male figures older than their early forties.

claims.statement: Nature's quiet would likely be temporary: as survivors restore transport and industry, noise and traffic would return, just as the 2020 seismic quieting lasted months rather than years and Bay of Fundy ship noise rose again after 2001.
claims.reasoning: Analogy to the months-long 2020 quiet period (CL05) and the post-2001 rebound in shipping noise and whale stress hormones (CL10).
claims.presentation_guardrail: The S10 time-lapse brings traffic and ambience back; never imply a permanent ecological recovery.

creative_direction.logline: In one silent second every man and boy on Earth vanishes. Following the sound of a changed planet, from a half-empty crosswalk to quiet seas and singing sparrows, the film finds that humanity survives and that men return within nine months as baby boys.
creative_direction.visual_identity: Premium natural-history realism for every place (city, port, interiors, ocean, nursery), intercut with restrained, clearly tagged glass-and-light schematics for numbers (ribbon chart, token meter, seismic trace, glass population pyramid). Recurring motif: human activity drawn as pale sound rings. Engine rings shrink as the world quiets; birdsong and whale-call rings grow. People are stylised, individuated figures (humanoid-figure-v1) seen at a respectful distance; absence is shown through empty chairs and left-behind objects, never bodies. No gender color-coding (no pink or blue) and no costume stereotypes; age and individuality come from proportions, posture, gait and accessories.
creative_direction.lighting: Motivated, physically plausible light only. City: blue-hour skylight plus 3000 K street lamps, warm 2700–3500 K windows and vehicle practicals. Orbit: dusk sunlight on the left of the limb, Black Marble night lights on the right. Interiors: dimmed 4500 K hospital panels with one warm desk lamp; red low-level light and screen glow on the ship's bridge. Ocean: sun shafts through a Snell window and green-blue fog. Sparrow: soft morning sun. Ending: dawn, then the time-lapse back to blue hour. Electricity stays on after T0 because lighting is automated, so lit windows and streetlights remain in every post-T0 city shot. Scene-referred HDR with ACES tone mapping (film-pipeline-v1); bloom only on true light sources; no fake lens flares.
creative_direction.camera_language: Unhurried documentary camera on camera-keyframe-rig-v1: slow push-ins, lateral trucks, one crane-up from street to orbit and one continuous pull-back from a nursery to the city. Lenses: 12–22° vertical FOV for intimate telephoto (sparrow, newborn, port), 28–40° for human-scale scenes, 44–50° underwater. No handheld shake and no whip pans. Ease semantics: each keyframe's ease shapes the segment that ends at it; two-keyframe shots repeat the same ease on both keys, and holds are authored as two identical keyframes, so either rig convention gives the intended motion. The last keyframe of S10 SH02 is identical to the first keyframe of S01 SH01, closing the loop.
creative_direction.motion_language: Everything is a pure function of absolute time (deterministic_frame_by_frame). Motion is slow and organic: walking at 1.25–1.45 m/s with analytic gait phase; machines decelerate along smooth envelopes rather than stopping dead; whales fluke about every 4 s; sound rings expand at a visual 6–40 m/s and fade with spherical spreading. Data schematics animate with ease_in_out_cubic over 0.5–1.2 s and then hold long enough to read. Time-lapses keep any light oscillation at or below 1.5 Hz with motion blur, so nothing strobes.
creative_direction.world_scale_policy: Real scale by default: 1 unit = 1 m in city, port, interior, sparrow and underwater shots; 1 unit = 1,000 km for Earth (radius 6.371). Earth is never enlarged and the Sun stays off-frame. Reference sizes: right whale adult 14 m and calf 5 m; white-crowned sparrow 0.16 m; container ship 300 m; ship-to-shore gantry crane 55 m; newborn hand about 6 cm. Deliberate deviations are tagged on screen: the port is filmed as an ILLUSTRATIVE tilt-shift diorama; the ribbon chart, token meter, seismic trace, sound rings, ground cross-section, birth glints and glass pyramid are SCHEMATIC or ILLUSTRATIVE; underwater visibility (about 35–45 m) is illustrative; song-ring radii are illustrative.
emotional_arc: Stillness and disbelief (0–12 s): a crosswalk half-empties without a sound
Understanding (12–26 s): why the world would go quiet, and proof that it can
Grief with dignity (26–36 s): absence in nearly every home while care continues
Unexpected wonder (36–49 s): whales and sparrows answer the quiet
Hope (49–66 s): men return as baby boys and a new generation rises
Resolution and loop (66–75 s): grief, rebuilding and an ordinary street again
creative_direction.opening_hook: Frame 0 is an ordinary, busy crosswalk at blue hour just after rain. At 0.9 s about half the pedestrians, including two children, fade in place; an umbrella drops, a walked bicycle tips over, and the survivors slow and look around. The spoken and captioned question lands by 3.05 s: 'What if every man on Earth disappeared?' No logo, greeting or call to action.
creative_direction.ending_payoff: A clear answer: humanity survives, smaller, grieving and rebuilding, while nature gets a temporary quiet. A curbside memorial and a women's repair crew at dawn give way to a decades-long time-lapse in which the crosswalk fills with a new, mixed generation: 'And one day, a busy street could look ordinary again.'
creative_direction.loop_connection: S10 SH02 ends on exactly the S01 frame-0 composition: the same camera keyframe (position [11.6, 1.55, 1.10], look_at [-4.0, 1.25, 0.15], FOV 30°), the same blue-hour lighting and wet asphalt, and the same 44-figure crowd state (pedestrian-crowd-v1 seed 'man-disappeared-crowd-01' at crowd clock τ = 0). The music decays fully by 74.8 s and the city bed matches t = 0, so a platform replay flows straight into the vanishing and the question.
creative_direction.asset_policy: reuse_before_create against assets/registry.json 1.0.0 (39 assets). Reuse 23 verified components (globe, NASA textures, stars, sky, clouds, ocean surface, underwater set, fish, birds, humanoid, bokeh, smoke, flame, grass, sailboat, dial gauge, captions, film pipeline, camera rig, labels, audio kit, shader math, Inter font) without cloning them; request only backward-compatible optional parameters whose defaults leave earlier films unchanged. Build 16 generalizable components into src/library/ and register them in assets/registry.json with created_for 'what-if-every-man-disappeared' only after the MP4 renders successfully. Keep the crowd seed, newborn-hand model, window tableaux, memorial and on-screen copy as shot-specific assets under src/stories/what-if-every-man-disappeared/. Story timing lives in src/stories/what-if-every-man-disappeared/film.ts, never inside library components.

audio.voice_style: Calm, peaceful, warm adult male; intimate documentary voice; natural breathing; wonder without shouting
audio.music_direction: Original procedural score from audio-synth-kit-v1 (no samples, no subscriptions), slow and D-centred. The first musical sound is a low felt-piano-like D2 with a long detuned pad at 2.0 s. Sparse three-note motifs mark the mechanism; a warm minor-sixth pad carries the grief (26–36 s); brighter open fifths for whales and sparrows; a modulation from D minor to F major at 'But men wouldn't stay gone' (about 51 s); a held F-major chord on 'just twenty' (about 64 s). The ending returns to the opening D voicing and decays fully by 74.8 s, so a replay starts on the same bare city bed as t = 0. Restrained bass (high-pass at 45 Hz, no sub drops) and no percussion except soft woodblock ticks in the S09 time-lapse. Music ducks a further 6 dB under narration with 150 ms attack and 600 ms release.
audio.sfx_direction: All SFX are procedural (audio-synth-kit-v1) or license-cleared CC0/CC-BY recordings with attribution stored beside the file in assets/library; no paid libraries. audio_cues.relative_db is relative to the narration's integrated level (0 dB = voice). Sound follows physical cause: the city bed thins as figures fade; port machines wind down with pitch-dropping motors; the underwater ship drone fades as the propeller stops; the whale upcall and sparrow song sit at -18 dB or lower under the voice or in its gaps. One soft air rush on the crane-up is the only whoosh in the film. No sirens, crashes, screams or crying sounds. Narration stays dominant and intelligible at all times.

captions.style: Elegant documentary kinetic captions rendered with caption-kinetic-v1: Inter SemiBold in warm white #F7F3EA, a 4 px dark stroke (#0B1322 at 55%), a soft drop shadow (0 3 px 12 px at 50%), and a feathered behind-text band (#0B1322 at 35% fading to 0) used only over bright backgrounds. Clause-aware 2–6-word phrases in at most two balanced lines; each phrase fades in over 120 ms with an 8 px upward settle; no bouncing and no per-letter animation. Numbers appear exactly as written in narration.text ('1975', '2020', '9/11').
captions.font_stack: Inter SemiBold 600 (font-inter-v1), Inter Medium 500, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Arial, sans-serif
captions.active_word_treatment: The word being spoken brightens from 88% to 100% white and gains a 2 px warm underline glow (#F2B66D at 45%) that glides to the next word, using word timings from tools/narrate.mjs (synthesized voice aligned with local Whisper), never guessed timings. No karaoke color wipes and no scaling of non-emphasized words. The caption block is centered at x = 540 with a maximum width of 800 px, keeping it clear of TikTok and Reels right-rail buttons (x > 950).
captions.highlights_policy: Only phrases listed in a scene's caption_emphasis are highlighted, at most one at a time: accent_color = #F2B66D fill; gentle_scale = 104% over 200 ms, then settle; subtle_glow = soft 10 px warm outer glow. Every emphasized phrase is an exact, case-sensitive substring of narration.text. In-scene callouts and SCHEMATIC / ILLUSTRATIVE / MEASURED tags (overlay-labels-v1) stay between y = 240 and 1180 px and never sit under the caption block; every crucial reveal is composed inside y = 260–1180 px.

narration.text: What if every man on Earth disappeared?
narration.delivery_note: Gentle, intimate and unhurried; a slight lift on 'disappeared', then let the question hang. 7 spoken words in about 2.9 s.

scenes.viewer_question: Wait, what would actually happen if every man vanished right now?
scenes.visual_payoff: A busy blue-hour crosswalk loses about half its pedestrians in one silent second: figures fade in place, an umbrella drops, a walked bicycle tips over, and the survivors slow to a stop and look around.

shots.shot_type: Low-angle telephoto push-in along a crosswalk (establishing hook)
shots.world: Invented mid-size city intersection (no real landmarks or brands) at blue hour just after light rain, late autumn. 1 unit = 1 m, Y up. Origin at the centre of the zebra crossing; pedestrians cross along X (curbs at X = ±7), traffic runs along Z, the crossing band spans Z −1.5..+1.5. Sidewalks are 5 m wide (X ±7..±12); 5–9-storey facades start at X = ±12. Cars wait at stop lines Z = ±4 with headlights on; pedestrian signals show WALK.

camera.movement: Slow 0.9 m dolly push along −X from the near curb with a 3 cm drop in eye height; starts from rest, which keeps the loop seam invisible.
camera.lens_notes: 30° vertical FOV (about 17° horizontal) compresses the crowd in depth so the gaps read instantly; focus at 9 m with gentle falloff (f/4 equivalent); a near-curb puddle in the lowest third catches reflections.

subjects.appearance: Wet charcoal asphalt with puddles mirroring amber lamps and red tail-lights; crisp, slightly worn white zebra stripes; granite curbs; shopfront glow; facades with about 55% of windows lit warm.
subjects.geometry_and_material: Procedural street block: asphalt PBR (roughness 0.35, puddle mask at roughness 0.04 with planar reflection), stripe decals with wear noise, instanced window quads with emissive 2700–3500 K variation, lamp posts with emissive heads and spot lights, unbranded stationary cars.
subjects.scale_and_accuracy: True scale: road 14 m wide; stripes 0.5 m wide by 3.0 m long with 0.5 m gaps; curb 0.15 m; storeys 3.2 m; lamp poles 8 m tall every 25 m.
subjects.movement: Static set; puddles ripple from awning drips at seeded times; the WALK signal starts blinking at 2.8 s.

subjects.appearance: 44 individuated pedestrians of many ages, heights, builds and skin tones in muted autumn layers (coats, scarves, hoodies), 9 open umbrellas, totes, backpacks and one person walking a bicycle; two pairs hold hands, one of them an adult with a child. No gender-coded costume or colour.
subjects.geometry_and_material: humanoid-figure-v1 instances driven by pedestrian-crowd-v1; matte fabric (roughness 0.8) with a slight rain sheen on shoulders; skin with wrap lighting; stylised faces never seen in close-up.
subjects.scale_and_accuracy: Adults 1.52–1.92 m drawn from realistic overlapping height distributions; 5 children 1.10–1.45 m via humanoid-age-proportions-v1; walking speeds 1.25–1.45 m/s.
subjects.movement: Cross in both directions on analytic gait cycles from seed 'man-disappeared-crowd-01' (crowd clock τ = t); survivors decelerate after the fade.

subjects.appearance: The 22 flagged figures (about half, including 2 children) fade in place: edges erode first, a faint warm rim, then a few soft motes that drift sideways on the breeze and disappear.
subjects.geometry_and_material: vanish-dissolve-v1 applied to the same meshes (noise-threshold alpha, rim #FFE9C9 at intensity 0.6), at most 40 additive motes per figure at 2–4 px.
subjects.scale_and_accuracy: In the story the removal is instantaneous; the 0.7 s per-figure dissolve is a visual convention.
subjects.movement: Each dissolve starts at 0.90 s plus a seeded 0–0.35 s offset and lasts 0.70 s; motes drift +X at 0.15 m/s and fade within 1.0 s; no upward 'ascension' motion.

subjects.appearance: A navy umbrella, a canvas tote, a phone and a green city bike left behind by vanished figures.
subjects.geometry_and_material: Simple PBR props parented to hand anchors until detach time; wet roughness 0.3.
subjects.scale_and_accuracy: Umbrella canopy 1.0 m across; bicycle 1.75 m long; drop heights from the hand 0.8–1.1 m.
subjects.movement: Detached at each owner's dissolve start; analytic free fall (t = √(2h/g), about 0.40–0.47 s) with a damped bounce of at most 4 cm; the umbrella rolls at most 0.3 m; the bicycle tips about its tyre contact line over 0.6 s and settles 2 cm.

subjects.appearance: Deep blue gradient above the rooftops, a faint warm city glow at the horizon, no visible sun.
subjects.geometry_and_material: sky-dome-v1 with sunIntensity 0 and sunGlow 0; zenith #0E1B33, horizon #2B4A73, haze #3A5578 at amount 0.25; toEnvironment() bakes the reflections.
subjects.scale_and_accuracy: Civil twilight, sun about 5° below the horizon.
subjects.movement: Static.

subjects.appearance: Six grey birds lifting off a cornice after the bicycle clatters.
subjects.geometry_and_material: bird-flock-v1 with bodyColor #7E848C, wingColor #8D939A, tipColor #3B3F45.
subjects.scale_and_accuracy: Wingspan 0.65 m; ledge 12 m above the street.
subjects.movement: Take off at 2.30 s and climb across the frame toward −Z; analytic flap phase easing from 6 Hz to 4 Hz.

animation_plan: 0.00–0.90 s: an ordinary crossing; the crowd walks on seed 'man-disappeared-crowd-01'; umbrellas bob with each gait cycle.
0.90–1.95 s: the 22 flagged figures dissolve in place with seeded 0–0.35 s staggers of 0.70 s each; held props detach at each start and fall analytically.
1.10–1.50 s: an adult's hand closes on the empty air where a child's hand was (reachArm toward the last hand position, weight 1.0 easing to 0.6).
1.60–2.40 s: the 22 survivors slow to a stop over 0.6–0.8 s (no running); heads turn up to ±25°; a few turn back toward where companions were.
1.85 s: the walked bicycle finishes tipping onto the stripes; 2.30 s: the pigeons lift off.
2.80–3.30 s: the WALK signal starts blinking; the camera continues its slow push.
shots.lighting: Blue-hour skylight from the sky-dome-v1 environment (intensity 0.6); six 3000 K street-lamp spot lights (8 m high, 45° cones) as key; warm shopfront area lights at sidewalk level as fill; 4500 K headlights and red tail-lights as practicals reflected in puddles; the pedestrian signal adds a small cool-green accent. Soft PCF shadows and contact shadows under feet and dropped props.
effects: film-pipeline-v1 ACES grade, exposure −0.2 EV, bloom on lamps and headlights only (threshold 1.1, strength 0.35)
vanish-dissolve-v1 rim glow and sideways motes
puddle ripple normal-map rings at seeded drip times
light exponential fog (density 0.012) for depth separation

A near-left figure at about (6.0, 0, 1.2) frames the left edge (torso at x ≈ 260 px); the adult-and-child pair walks at about (−2.0, 0, 0.2), so the hand-closing moment lands near x ≈ 560, y ≈ 1110 px. No on-screen text except the caption.

audio_cues.description: Blue-hour city bed: tyre hiss on wet road, footsteps, soft unintelligible murmur and a crossing-signal tick.
Footsteps and murmur thin out with the fade; a faint airy shimmer (pink noise through a slow high-shelf sweep) sits under the dissolve.
Soft, damped clatter of the umbrella and then the bicycle settling on wet asphalt (procedural, slightly distant).
The first musical sound: a low felt-piano-like D2 blooming into a long pad with the A2 fifth above.

transition_out.motivation: Continuous camera: S02 SH01 starts from S01's final keyframe and cranes straight up, so the crowd we just saw stays in frame as the scale opens.

narration.text: Over four billion men and boys, gone in an instant. Humanity shrinks to about its size in 1975.
narration.delivery_note: Calm and factual, with a brief pause after 'instant'. Pronounce '1975' as 'nineteen seventy-five' (captions keep '1975'). 19 spoken words in about 7.9 s.

scenes.viewer_question: How many people is that, really?
scenes.visual_payoff: The camera rises from the stilled crosswalk through the clouds to Earth's twilight limb, where a glass population ribbon drops from 8.30 to 4.13 billion and slides back to 1975.

shots.shot_type: Continuous crane-up from street level to above the cloud deck
shots.world: The same intersection moments after T0 (22 survivors standing, props on the ground), then the surrounding city out to a 3 km radius: every window and streetlight still lit, traffic stopped at intersections, no collisions shown. A cloud deck sits at 1,800 m. 1 unit = 1 m; origin at the crossing centre.

camera.movement: Accelerating crane-up: altitude grows roughly 3× per keyframe (1.5 m to 2.3 km) and slows slightly at the end above the deck. If camera-keyframe-rig-v1 can interpolate this shot along a Catmull-Rom path with altitude in log space, use that; otherwise the dense linear keys approximate it.
camera.lens_notes: Keeps S01's 30° FOV so the move reads as one continuous shot; the far plane must reach 60 km for the cloud deck horizon; logarithmic depth buffer recommended.

subjects.appearance: Grid of mid-rise blocks at blue hour, warm windows, amber streetlights, stopped cars with headlights on, a river of light where avenues meet.
subjects.geometry_and_material: city-street-block-v1 near set plus instanced far-field LOD blocks with emissive window textures; distance haze.
subjects.scale_and_accuracy: Blocks 80–120 m; avenues 20–30 m wide; true scale to 3 km.
subjects.movement: Static; lights stay on.

subjects.geometry_and_material: Same pedestrian-crowd-v1 instances and props as S01.
subjects.movement: Idle breathing and small head turns; the embrace forms at 3.6–4.4 s.

subjects.appearance: Twilight cloud tops in deep blue with a warm band at the horizon, seen only after the camera breaks through.
subjects.geometry_and_material: cloud-deck-v1 at level 1800 m, coverage 0.6; below it, scene fog ramps to a brief white-out while the camera passes through.

subjects.movement: Scroll offsets drift 2 m/s; visible from 6.55 s.

subjects.appearance: Large callout '4.17 BILLION' in warm bone with the small tag 'men and boys · UN WPP 2024'.
subjects.geometry_and_material: overlay-labels-v1 callout anchored by projectToScreen() to a point above the horizon line.
subjects.movement: Fades in 4.90–5.30 s, holds, fades out by 6.30 s.

4.50–5.70 s: the city grid opens: every streetlight and window still lit, traffic stopped at intersections.
4.90–6.30 s: callout '4.17 BILLION' with tag 'men and boys · UN WPP 2024' fades in at y ≈ 420 px, holds and fades out.
6.30–6.55 s: scene fog ramps to a cloud white-out as the camera passes the 1,800 m deck; 6.55–6.70 s: twilight cloud tops below, then the frame brightens toward white for the light wipe into SH02.
shots.lighting: Inherits S01's blue-hour rig at street level; above 200 m the city reads by its own emissive lights; the cloud deck takes faint warm afterglow from the west and cool skylight from above.
effects: altitude-dependent fog (density keyed 0.012 to 0.0004, then a 0.25 s white-out in cloud)
motion blur from the camera's own motion (4 deterministic sub-frames)
shots.composition_notes: The crossing stays near frame centre for the first second, then the city fills the lower two-thirds; the callout sits in the sky band above y ≈ 520 px; the white-out hides the cut to orbit.

shots.shot_type: Slow orbital drift over Earth's twilight limb with a schematic ribbon chart
shots.world: Earth seen from about 2,600 km above the dusk terminator, night side to the right. 1 unit = 1,000 km; Earth (radius 6.371) at the origin; earth-globe-v1 setView(10°E, 0°) puts central Europe near the limb crest at about 48°N with Black Marble city lights; sunDirection normalize(−0.97, 0.0, −0.24) lights the left third of the limb. All city lights stay on (nightOutage 0). Stars behind.

camera.movement: Slow lateral drift of 1,100 km with a slight rise; the limb crest stays near y ≈ 1200 px.
camera.lens_notes: 34° vertical FOV; Earth is physically scaled (angular radius about 42°), so only the limb arc is in frame. The chart renders in a camera-locked overlay layer, not in world space.

subjects.appearance: Twilight limb: blue daylit ocean and cloud on the left, a warm terminator, and Europe's and North Africa's city lights on the night side to the right; thin blue atmospheric rim.
subjects.geometry_and_material: earth-globe-v1 with earth-textures-nasa-v1 (Blue Marble day, Black Marble night lights, clouds, land mask), atmosphere shell, ocean glint.
subjects.scale_and_accuracy: Radius 6.371 units (6,371 km); camera altitude about 2,600 km; atmosphere rim thickness true to scale.
subjects.movement: Linear spin at 0.02°/s and default cloud drift from update(time_s).

subjects.appearance: Sparse, natural starfield, dimmer near the bright limb.
subjects.geometry_and_material: starfield-v1 point sprites.
subjects.movement: Follows the camera (no parallax).

subjects.appearance: Glass panel holding a glowing warm-bone line with a faint area fill: world population 1950–2026, gridlines at 2, 4, 6 and 8 billion, ticks at 1950, 1975, 2000 and 2026, endpoint label '8.30 B · 2026', tag 'SCHEMATIC · UN WPP 2024'.
subjects.geometry_and_material: population-ribbon-chart-v1 in a camera-locked overlay scene (FOV 34°): panel 0.76 m × 0.59 m centred at (0, 0.30, −3.0) m, frosted glass (alpha 0.18), emissive line width 6 px, labels via overlay-labels-v1.

subjects.movement: Draws on, drops its endpoint, slides a lookup line back to 1975.

animation_plan: 6.70–7.10 s: white haze clears to reveal the twilight limb (continuation of the light wipe).
7.10–7.80 s: the chart panel fades in (0.5 s) while the ribbon draws from 1950 to 2026 (ease_in_out_cubic).
8.20–8.90 s: on 'Humanity shrinks', the 2026 endpoint drops from 8.30 B to 4.13 B (ease_in_out_cubic); a ghost dot stays at 8.30 B and the label updates to '4.13 B'.
9.10–10.40 s: a dashed lookup line slides left at the 4.13 B level until it meets the curve near 1975.
10.40–11.50 s: a marker pulses at 1975 with the label '1975 · 4.07 B'; Earth keeps its slow linear spin.
11.50–11.90 s: hold; the night-side city lights begin the cross-dissolve to the port.
shots.lighting: Directional sunlight from normalize(−0.97, 0.0, −0.24) at physical intensity with ACES exposure −0.3 EV; atmospheric rim scattering; night lights emissive; the overlay panel is unlit (emissive line only).

audio_cues.description: One soft, low air rush that follows the crane's speed (band-passed brown noise, slow sweep); the only whoosh in the film.
The S01 city bed thins with altitude and is gone by 6.2 s.
Soft cloud hiss during the white-out.
Orbit: no ambience bed and no fake space sounds; only the music pad and narration.
Gentle descending glass tone as the endpoint drops to 4.13 B.
The pad opens a fifth higher as the 1975 marker pulses.

transition_out.motivation: Earth's night-side city lights dissolve into the warm floodlights of a port at dusk: from the whole planet to one place where work happens.

narration.text: Men hold six in ten of the world's paid jobs. Overnight, countless engines would stop.
narration.delivery_note: Clear and explanatory; slight weight on 'six in ten'; a short breath before 'Overnight'; let 'stop' fall softly. 15 spoken words in about 6.25 s.

scenes.viewer_question: Why would the world suddenly change so much?
scenes.visual_payoff: Six of ten glowing job tokens dim over a working port; then cranes, trucks and a chimney wind down to stillness while every light stays on, and a gull lands on the silent crane.

audio_cues.description: Port at work: crane motor whine, diesel yard tractors, soft reversing beeps, harbor water lapping, one short distant ship horn.
Six soft descending glass ticks as six tokens dim.
Machines wind down one by one: motor whine pitch-drops, diesels idle off, belt rattle stops; only water lapping and a faint transformer hum remain.
A single distant gull call as it lands.

transition_out.motivation: The quieted port sinks into darkness and resolves on an underground vault: we go below the stillness to where the ground's vibrations are measured.

narration.text: We've had a preview: in 2020, the ground itself grew quieter—in places, by half.
narration.delivery_note: Quiet wonder; a small pause after 'preview'. Pronounce '2020' as 'twenty twenty'. Land softly on 'by half'. 16 spoken words in about 6.6 s.

scenes.viewer_question: Is there any real evidence for what a quieter world looks like?
scenes.visual_payoff: A seismometer's glowing trace calms to half its height; then a cross-section shows the vibrations under a near-empty 2020 street shrinking, with a bracket reading 'up to −50% · some stations'.

audio_cues.description: Low, steady ground rumble (40–80 Hz, gentle) standing in for human-made vibration; filtered so it never masks the voice.
The rumble halves in level and smooths out.
2020 street at dusk: sparse distant traffic, a bird or two, open quiet air.
Soft three-note piano figure resolving on 'by half'.

transition_out.motivation: The lit windows above the 2020 street dissolve into the lit windows of homes after T0: from measured quiet to the human cost.

narration.text: For people, history's greatest loss—nearly every family, grieving at once. Hospitals would keep most of their staff; cargo ships, almost none.

scenes.viewer_question: What would daily life be like for the people left?

audio_cues.description: A short hush before the twist: music and ambience dip.
Nursery at night: soft ventilation, a distant gentle monitor chime, tiny newborn breaths (very soft).
The hopeful turn: the pad modulates from D minor to F major under a rising four-note felt-piano figure.
Night-city air: distant wind and a faint traffic hum returning.

narration.text: Then births would plunge, sustained by sperm banks. Twenty years on, the oldest man on Earth would be just twenty.

audio_cues.description: Dawn: a few birds, a distant bus idling, soft clinks of tools from the bucket truck; the candles are silent.
Time-lapse texture: the city soundscape rises from sparse to busy (footsteps, murmur, tyre hiss) and crossfades into the exact S01 opening bed by 74.6 s.
Resolution: the opening felt-piano D returns over a warm pad and decays completely by 74.8 s, so the replay starts on the bare city bed as at t = 0.
Loop seam: the city bed's level and spectrum matched to t = 0.0 (no fade to silence).

transition_out.motivation: The last frame equals frame 0 (same camera keyframe, crowd state, lighting and city bed), so a platform loop continues seamlessly into the vanishing and the question.

distribution.primary_search_intent: what would happen if all men disappeared
core_keywords: what if every man on earth disappeared
distribution.distinctive_angle: A calm, evidence-first thought experiment that follows the sound of a changed planet: real data on jobs, hospitals and shipping; measured wildlife responses to past human pauses (Bay of Fundy 2001, 2020 lockdowns); and the twist that men would return within nine months as tens of millions of baby boys, so twenty years later the oldest man alive would be twenty.
distribution.seo_integrity_note: Final titles, descriptions and hashtags are written by the rendering agent only after a successful MP4 and must match the rendered narration. Do not promise extinction, battle-of-the-sexes outcomes, utopia, dystopia or anything the film does not show; keep the 'thought experiment' framing and credit UN WPP 2024, ILO, ILO–WHO, BIMCO/ICS, Rolland et al. 2012, Lecocq et al. 2020, Derryberry et al. 2020 and NASA imagery in descriptions. Independent, truthful platform hooks (the schema has no per-platform field, so they live here): YouTube Shorts: 'What if every man on Earth disappeared? Real science and one surprising twist.' TikTok: 'Every man vanishes. Nine months later…' Instagram Reels: 'A world without men would sound different. Here is the data.' Facebook Reels: 'Would humanity survive if every man disappeared? A gentle science thought experiment.' X video: 'If every man vanished: hospitals keep most staff, cargo ships almost none, whales get quieter seas. Then the twist.' No engagement bait, fake urgency or gendered insults.
